summary.headline: Shilchar Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 134.60 crore with EBITDA of Rs 29.23 crore and PAT of Rs 20.86 crore, hit by West Asia shipping costs and slow price pass-through.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 134.60 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 29.23 crore and PAT of Rs 20.86 crore. Management attributed the soft quarter to a sharp rise in container costs from the West Asia crisis, which delayed export dispatches, and to slow negotiations to pass on raw material price increases on domestic orders. Management said it lost roughly Rs 30-35 crore of potential revenue and that Q1 capacity utilisation was about 60-65%. It maintained FY27 guidance (Rs 800 crore revenue was referenced by an analyst, not reiterated as a number) and expects Q2 to be notably better than Q1, with Phase-3 expansion (6,500 MVA) due for commissioning in April 2027.

financial_highlights.change: Computed from EBITDA/revenue; management did not state it. Historical margin cited by analyst as about 30%

financial_highlights.metric: Estimated revenue lost to shipment delays
financial_highlights.change: Management estimate; declined to call it revenue loss
Over and above shipments made until the call date; about 70% domestic, 30% export

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Export dispatches slowed as container costs rose three to five times for some geographies versus pre-crisis levels; management says customers are buying only minimum volumes, not cancelling. Export is about 90% of export orders on an ex-works basis per management, and the order book is about 30% export.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic dispatches were slowed by negotiations to pass on raw material price escalation on existing orders, with April and May the worst months and conditions easing since. Management says domestic market is normal versus last year and no lower-margin pressure in lower KV classes; order book is about 70% domestic.

guidance_outlook: FY27 annual outlook unchanged; management says it is on track for the top-line target and expects no problem achieving it, though geographic mix may shift if West Asia persists.
Q2 FY27 business momentum expected to be notably better than Q1; domestic visibility better, exports may stay impacted by shipping costs.
Existing 7,500 MVA capacity to run at near full utilisation in FY27; management targets close to 100% utilisation for FY27.
EBITDA: management does not expect problems achieving EBITDA as Q2 orders are at current raw material prices; expects Q2 EBITDA higher than Q1 but gave no margin percentage.

Phase-3 expansion (about 6,500 MVA) on track for commissioning in April 2027; new facility to drive growth from FY28; bigger-KV transformer orders expected later due to customer audits, approvals and type testing.
Margin normalisation depends on exports returning; if domestic-heavy mix persists, margins could dip slightly. New capacity to carry lower initial margins to build references.
capex_capacity: Phase-3 expansion adds about 6,500 MVA; commissioning targeted April 2027, possibly slightly earlier than projected.
Civil foundation work complete; PEB erection and utility work progressing; all equipment ordered.
Additional about 4.5 acres of land bought adjacent to existing Gavasad site for future expansion; product and KV class not yet disclosed.
Prototyping for larger transformers takes about 3-4 months after production starts; discussions under way with a few customers on bigger units.
Company will not supply state utility companies; plans to focus on exports once domestic references are established.
demand_pricing: Management says underlying demand in both export and domestic markets remains firm; customers are buying minimum volumes due to freight costs and uncertainty.
Export orders being deferred, not cancelled; management says delivery dates pushed by about 1-2 months (e.g., June to July or August).
Only 50-60% of raw material price rise passed on to customers for orders in hand from Q4 and Q1; current orders priced at current market prices.
Lead time for custom transformers is about 10-16 weeks; management says customers prefer Shilchar on quality, service and shorter lead time.
Management says competition is not the issue for exports: customers are not buying from rivals, just holding purchases.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify Q1 revenue loss from shipment delays and whether FY27 Rs 800 crore guidance is being revisited.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to call it a loss but said Rs 30-35 crore could have been done without the crisis; it reiterated FY27 top-line target with no anticipated problem.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material cost increase was passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50-60% of the price rise was passed on for orders from Q4 and Q1; current execution is at market prices so EBITDA is not expected to be a problem.

qa_highlights.question: Order book size and domestic/export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book close to Rs 500 crore over and above shipments to date; about 70% domestic and 30% export; mostly for Q2, Q3 and some Q4, with Q2 fully booked.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins stay near 30% EBITDA, and will the 220 KV expansion be lower margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins can match prior years if exports recover; otherwise a slight dip. New 220 KV-class capacity will carry lower initial margins to build references, with better margins later.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 export focus not shifted to domestic earlier, leaving capacity underused?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shipping was normal in April but costs spiked from late April/May; it shifted focus to domestic promptly, but custom orders take time to win and execute, benefits showing in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Q1 capacity utilisation and export/domestic revenue split and receivable/inventory days?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 utilisation was about 60-65%; export/domestic revenue split and inventory and receivable days were not disclosed on the call and will be sent by email.

risks_watch: Persistent West Asia conflict keeping container costs elevated (three to five times pre-crisis for some routes) and delaying export orders.
Q1 EBITDA margin (about 21.7% implied) well below the roughly 30% historically cited; Q2 margin recovery depends on domestic price pass-through and mix.
Phase-3 commissioning slippage in April 2027, and ramp-up of larger KV transformers which need customer approval and type testing.
Management's earlier outlook in the FY26 annual report (prepared early June) assumed normalisation that did not happen; credibility of outlook is a watch item.
Export revenue permanence: management says orders are deferred, not lost, but this is unverified; monitor Q2 export dispatches and order book conversion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term demand and FY27 targets, but cautious and at times evasive on specifics: declined to quantify margins, the export/domestic split for revenue, and inventory/receivable days, and repeatedly referred the latter to email. The tone shifted from the prior view that Middle East normalisation would come quickly.
